Reserved on : 07.08.2024 Delivered on : 14.08.2024 Court No. - 74 Case :- APPLICATION U/S 482 No. - 10633 of 2024 Applicant :- Alok Kumar Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Archana Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kamlesh Singh Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.

Heard Smt. Archana Singh, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Kamlesh Singh, learned counsel for opposite party No.2.
2.
The complainant in the present case, is a widow whereas the applicant is her step brother-in-law.

It was a case of complainant that her husband died on 05.08.2013 and she executed a gift deed in favour of present applicant on 5 March, 2021 and as soon as she realised that the said gift deed was executed purportedly convincing her that she has put her thumb impression on a document of pension, thereafter she filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. on 02.07.2021, which was considered to be a criminal complaint.
3. Learned Trial Court after considering the statements recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. summoned the applicant to face trial for an offence under Section 420 I.P.C. in Complaint Alok Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131032502/
1 Case No.10409 of 2021, Police Station- Shahganj, District- Agra.

4. Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that gift deed was executed by complainant in his favour on her own will without any coercion or pressure or misrepresentation.

The said gift deed was not challenged before any Civil Court and only in order to cloak a criminal case to a dispute which was essentially of a civil nature, the present criminal proceedings were initiated.

5. The aforesaid submissions are opposed by learned counsel for opposite party No.2 that it was a case where a widow was cheated and applicant has fraudulently and dishonestly induced her to put thumb impression on papers believed to be supposedly of pension but later on she found it was a gift deed and promptly she then lodged a criminal complaint.
6.
He further refers that amount of house about Rs.44 lakh and that there is no other livelihood of the complainant.
Heard counsel for parties and perused the record.

7. It is not under dispute that on a particular dispute both civil and criminal action could be taken.
In the present case, cancellation of a gift deed is a civil dispute, however, the statement made by complainant i.e. a widow under Section 200 Cr.P.C. has become relevant and for reference the same is reproduced hereinafter :-

8. The aforesaid statement of complainant was being completely corroborated by statement of witnesses recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. If the statement of complainant is taken as a whole as well as considering that she is a widow, she has not other property as well as she has no other means of livelihood, therefore, to make a gift deed of this residential home which is about of Rs. 44 lakh on face of it appears to be a fraudulent act.

9. In the aforesaid circumstances, since statement of widow is consistent that she was under believe that she has put thumb impression on documents in regard to pension of her husband but since she found that it was a gift deed, she immediately filed an application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.
which is her bonafide action, therefore, it is not a case where the complainant has attempted to make a cloak of criminal case to a dispute of which is essentially a civil dispute but it is a case where prima facie case of cheating is made out that the applicant has induced the complainant to sign a gift deed believing it to be a document of a pension.

In the aforesaid circumstances, I do not find that it is a case where any interference could be caused in impugned summoning order and accordingly,
present application is rejected.
